stories.body: Yemeni government forces, backed by extensive Saudi-led coalition air support, launched a major offensive around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait and said they had secured the waterway, captured Dhubab airfield and taken or reached the outskirts of Mokha. Houthi officials denied losing control of Bab al-Mandab, Mokha or Dhubab, while also claiming attacks on Riyadh airport and other Saudi targets in retaliation. The fighting comes after recent Houthi gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast and near Taiz, and the government says operations have begun on several fronts, including around Sanaa. The UN warned of a sharp escalation, while Turkey and Pakistan reportedly agreed in Riyadh to deploy forces to Saudi Arabia under their joint defence arrangement.
stories.headline: Saudi-backed forces and Houthis escalate fighting around Yemen's Bab al-Mandab Strait

stories.body: A student protest movement that began at a school in a low-income Paris suburb has spread across France, with hundreds of high schools barricaded or forced to close over teacher shortages, overcrowding, deteriorating buildings and inequality in education. Clashes have intensified, with police using water cannon in Rennes and human rights groups alleging disproportionate force against minors. The government says 215 teenagers, 715 police officers and 85 teaching staff have been injured, while the justice ministry reports more than 5,000 arrests since the protests began, most involving minors. Ten investigations into alleged police brutality are under way after serious injuries to young protesters.
stories.headline: French student protests spread nationwide amid clashes with police

stories.body: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks on Moscow in two years, killing two men and injuring several people in the Russian capital, according to local officials. Separately, drone strikes hit two merchant vessels in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea: a Turkish-owned cargo ship flying the Togolese flag sank and its crew remained missing, while the crew of a grain carrier was rescued, including two injured sailors. Bulgarian authorities have opened a search operation and condemned the attack as a violation of maritime law, though they did not publicly identify the attacker. The incidents underline the expanding risks to commercial shipping as the war increasingly affects the Black Sea.
stories.headline: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Moscow as Black Sea shipping comes under attack

stories.body: Kenya has recorded its first Ebola case and death after a Kenyan citizen who had lived in the Democratic Republic of Congo for seven years died in Nairobi. The man had been ill and treated in the DRC, travelled overland to Kampala and then flew to Nairobi on October 3, where he later tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain. Authorities have identified 28 close contacts and are tracing another 23 passengers and four crew members from his flight, while preparing a safe burial and quarantine measures. The case comes amid a severe DRC outbreak that the World Health Organization says has caused more than 4,000 deaths, with Médecins Sans Frontières warning of an alarming rise in cases in North Kivu.
stories.headline: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as the outbreak spreads from DR Congo

stories.body: Quebec's Parti Québécois has won enough seats to form a minority government, returning the separatist party to power for the first time since 2014. Its leader, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, has pledged an eventual referendum on independence, likely in 2029 or 2030 after Donald Trump's US presidency ends, although polling suggests only about 30% of Quebecers support separation and opposition parties reject another vote. The party fell short of a majority, leaving it dependent on other parties that may support it on some issues but not on independence. The outcome creates a new challenge for Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, including likely disputes with Quebec over immigration, language, identity and the monarchy.
stories.headline: Quebec separatists win election, promising a 2029 independence referendum

stories.body: German prosecutors have arrested August Hanning, the former head of the Federal Intelligence Service, or BND, on suspicion of espionage and treason. They allege that Hanning used classified intelligence to prepare an analysis for an officer from a foreign intelligence service and passed on political information to another foreign service contact. A former BND chief of staff, identified as Manfred D, was also arrested and is accused of supplying Hanning with roughly 2,000 classified documents in exchange for payment. Authorities have not named the foreign powers involved, and the investigation emerged from a separate inquiry linked to alleged child kidnappings involving a Hamburg business heiress.
stories.headline: Germany arrests former intelligence chief on espionage and treason allegations

stories.body: Belgian physicist Francis Halzen has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. Halzen developed the vision for using a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice, filled with thousands of light sensors, to detect the rare flashes produced when neutrinos interact with matter. Because neutrinos can pass through dense regions and are not bent by magnetic fields, their paths can help scientists trace violent, high-energy events in distant galaxies that conventional telescopes cannot readily observe. The Nobel committee said his scientific leadership opened the way to a new form of astronomy.
stories.headline: Francis Halzen wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for cosmic-neutrino research

stories.body: President Donald Trump has approved the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth recommended the execution, and the Army secretary will determine its date and location. If it proceeds after the required legal and appellate review, it would be the first execution carried out by the US military since 1961 and the first by military firing squad since the end of the Second World War. Hasan, who was sentenced to death in 2013, remains one of four inmates on military death row.
stories.headline: Trump approves firing-squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan

stories.body: AI-safety advocates are pressing OpenAI and candidates to go further than recent signals that company-linked political spending may be reduced. Sam Altman acknowledged that spending by industry-aligned groups such as the Leading the Future super PAC may have backfired, while OpenAI president Greg Brockman reportedly pulled back from further support for the group. Critics say that is insufficient while major technology investors and political groups can still spend heavily to influence AI policy. Leading the Future and the Anthropic-backed Public First network have together spent more than $70 million through super PACs this cycle, intensifying a debate over whether candidates should reject AI-industry support and whether competing groups should agree to scale back spending.
stories.headline: AI-safety advocates demand stronger limits on OpenAI-linked political spending

stories.body: An abnormally strong, potentially record-breaking El Niño could amplify California's winter weather, increasing the risk of extreme storms, flooding and coastal erosion. The eventual impact will vary by location and storm track, but the unusually warm Pacific conditions raise the prospect of a more volatile season for a state already exposed to damaging rain, waves and landslides.
stories.headline: Record-strength El Niño could intensify California's winter storms

stories.body: Spain's Constitutional Court has ruled that the Supreme Court must apply the amnesty law to the misuse-of-public-funds charges connected to Catalonia's 2017 independence push, finding that its refusal to do so in the case of former regional minister Dolors Bassa violated her right to effective judicial protection. The ruling establishes a doctrine that also applies to former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont and other pro-independence leaders. Soon after the decision, Supreme Court judge Pablo Llarena lifted the national arrest warrant that had applied to Puigdemont, Toni Comín and Lluís Puig since 2017, allowing Puigdemont to return to Spain without risk of arrest. The amnesty also opens the possibility for affected leaders to stand for election again.
stories.headline: Spain's Constitutional Court clears the way for Carles Puigdemont's return

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called an early general election for November 29, about eight months ahead of schedule, after Congress rejected his government's housing decrees. Sánchez framed the vote as a choice between a far-right rollback and a more open, socially just Spain, while the opposition Popular Party welcomed an election it had long demanded and Vox said it was ready to offer an alternative. Polls indicate that the Popular Party could win but may need Vox to govern. The announcement has forced parties into a compressed campaign timetable, with the left still reorganising its electoral platform and Catalan parties preparing for another consequential national contest.
stories.headline: Spain's parties begin campaigning after Sánchez calls a November 29 general election

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez's government has reapproved the two housing decrees that Congress rejected last week and plans to send them to the permanent parliamentary council during the election period. The package contains 21 measures and includes a €10 billion financing line for interest-free loans of up to €50,000 for people buying their first home, aimed at easing the savings barrier to obtaining a mortgage. The move follows nationwide housing protests and the eviction of an 87-year-old Madrid tenant that became a symbol of anger over the housing crisis. Sánchez called the November 29 election after his legislative defeat, as polls suggest a potential Popular Party and Vox majority.
stories.headline: Spain's government revives housing measures, including first-home loans, through the permanent council

stories.body: Catalonia remains under an emergency rainfall plan after a severe storm disrupted roads, rail services and public transport, with further torrential downpours forecast. Authorities are searching for a man reportedly swept away in Pineda de Mar and for a missing minor in Granollers, while two people died during the weekend storm in Tordera and Montornès del Vallès. Several roads remain closed or restricted, and Rodalies commuter rail has widespread disruption, with replacement buses on many routes and no rail service on the R7. Meteorologists warn that some areas could receive more than 40 litres of rain per square metre in 30 minutes, particularly later in the day along the coast and pre-coastal areas.
stories.headline: Catalonia faces renewed torrential-rain alerts after flooding disrupts roads and rail service

stories.body: Barcelona's city government plans to raise property tax on tourist apartments by as much as 150% once Spain's revived housing decrees are approved. The proposal would permit surcharges of up to 50% for one tourist flat, up to 100% for owners of two to four, and up to 150% for owners with four or more. Deputy mayor Jordi Valls said the policy is intended to discourage tourist accommodation until Barcelona's planned full ban on such flats takes effect in 2028. The city estimates the increase could raise about €7 million annually for protected housing, and the measure is expected to receive support from Barcelona en Comú and Esquerra Republicana.
stories.headline: Barcelona plans to raise property tax on tourist flats by up to 150%

stories.body: Spain's two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, have agreed to call a 24-hour general strike this autumn over housing affordability and wages, with the final date to be set in consultation with social organisations and tenants' groups. The action is expected before the formal election campaign begins on November 13 and would be the first general strike held during a national pre-election period. The unions say the strike will demand wages that allow people to afford decent housing and will target public administrations and employers. Business groups CEOE and Foment del Treball have criticised the plan, arguing that a housing protest is not a lawful basis for a general strike and promising to assess its legal footing once formally called.
stories.headline: Catalan unions call a general strike over housing ahead of Spain's election campaign

stories.body: A housing demonstration in central Barcelona ended in clashes between a group of protesters and Mossos d'Esquadra police after the main march was formally over. Authorities said protesters threw objects, fireworks, bottles, chairs and construction material, set containers and bicycles on fire, damaged shopfronts and police vehicles, and built barricades between Passeig de Gràcia and Plaça de Catalunya. At least 13 people were arrested, including one minor, and reports said 28 officers sustained minor injuries; Barcelona firefighters extinguished 22 fires and city officials put damage at more than €42,000. The unrest occurred near an ongoing housing protest camp in Plaça de Catalunya.
stories.headline: Barcelona housing demonstration ends in clashes, arrests and injuries to police
